archimate:Principle.name: orchestration
archimate:Principle.documentation:
CONTEXT
The Integration Layer Pilot proves three patterns on Azure Integration Services. For Orchestration, a consuming application calls a REST API through API Management, and the API returns data from the source system. The pilot uses a new read-only MOP API v1, hosted on AKS and secured with Entra ID OAuth 2.0, as the Orchestration Service described in the Integration Layer low-level design (v0.11). This also proves that a new API can be built to the HLD standards, including the DSA and GEMINI header tags, the canonical model and the standard error format.
The API is being built against a copy of the MOP Oracle database on an Azure VM. That copy works for pilot implementation only. The API cannot move to non-production or production.
PROPOSAL A snapshot of the MOP database copied to Azure, with MOP API v1 reading from the it as a temporary, read-only source.
The snapshot is the preferred option because the pilot is a proof of concept to prove the integration pattern, not to deliver a permanent data source, and it is the only option that fits the timeline. It is a temporary measure, and because the data source is configurable it can be replaced by a permanent source later without changing the API or its consumers.
How it would work - A snapshot copy the MOP data from the on-premise database to the Azure Oracle copy, reusing existing database copy jobs where possible. - MOP API v1 stays read-only and reads only from the Azure copy. - No new inbound connection is made to the on-premise database, and the end-of-life firewall is not changed. - PCS, L&C and TMS are not touched.
